Issued at 257 PM EDT Thu Oct 1 2026

Near Term through Tonight...

Afternoon satellite imagery shows mostly sunny skies across the 
region.  Breezy southwest winds have allowed temperatures to warm 
into the 86-89 degree range as of mid-afternoon.  With a few more 
hours of heating, we'll see temps top out in the upper 80s with a 
few spots breaking 90.  We expect the gusty winds to diminish toward 
sunset.  During the evening, we'll see high level cloud cover 
continue to increase from west to east while temperatures fall back 
into the 70s.  Clouds will continue thicken overnight while a cold 
frontal boundary approaches from the west.  Southwest low-level flow 
will continue overnight bringing added moisture into the region.  As 
the front approaches, showers will move into southwest Indiana after 
midnight, mainly between 2-5 AM.  Current thinking is that rainfall 
along/southeast of the Ohio River will hold off until after sunrise 
on Friday.  A tenth to quarter inch of rainfall is expected across 
southern Indiana overnight.  Lows will mainly be in the upper 60s in 
Indiana with mainly lower 70s across much of Kentucky.

Friday through Saturday Night...

Low amplitude trough axis will trek through the Great Lakes/Ohio 
Valley during the period.  As the trough passes, a surface cold 
front will slice through the region.  Widespread rain showers are 
expected across the outlook area during the day on Friday and into 
Friday Night.  Model proximity soundings continue show a relatively 
moist airmass characterized by weak low and mid-level lapse rates. 
Wind shear through the column also remains very weak.  Abundant 
cloud cover and ongoing precipitation will likely limit instability 
during day.  However, there may be localized pockets of instability 
that develop which may yield a few rumbles of thunder across the 
region.  At this time, the risk of severe weather is very low. Model 
soundings also show PWATs above 2 inches during the day, so any 
organized shower activity can put down some locally heavy rainfall. 
However, the recent dry spell across the region will allow this 
rainfall to infiltrate and hydrologic issues are not expected.  A 
solid half to one inch of rainfall is expected.  Highs on the day 
will vary depending on where the frontal boundary ends up.  Highs on 
the north side of the front will only reach the upper 60s to around 
70.  South of the front highs in the upper 70s to the lower 80s are 
expected.  Lows Friday night will drop into the lower 50s in Indiana 
with mid-upper 50s across Kentucky.  Our southern KY counties may 
stay just south of the front and may remain in the low 60s overnight.

For Saturday, upper trough axis will push off to the east while the 
upper flow becomes more zonal.  This will allow the front to push 
further southward as a wave of low pressure develops along it. 
Additional rounds of showers are likely for Saturday, mainly in 
areas south of the WK/BG Parkway.  Skies will be mostly cloudy with 
highs in the upper 60s to the lower 70s.  Some partial clearing may 
take place Saturday night as lows fall into the upper 40s/lower 50s 
over southern Indiana with mainly mid-upper 50s across Kentucky.

Sunday through Thursday...

Secondary upper trough axis will push through the region on Sunday 
and allow the cold front from the weekend to continue to push 
southward.  High pressure will build into the region from the 
Midwest.  For much of next week, the upper flow pattern will feature 
a ridge across the west with a downstream trough centered near the 
US east coast.  This will keep the Ohio Valley in a northwest to 
west-northwest flow aloft with seasonal fall temperatures.  Highs 
Sunday through Tuesday will feature highs in the upper 60s to around 
70 across southern Indiana and across the northern half of Kentucky. 
Southern Kentucky will see readings in the lower 70s.  We'll see 
large diurnal swings in temperatures as good radiational cooling is 
expected for Monday night and Tuesday night.  Lows Tuesday/Wednesday 
morning will likely drop into the upper 30s and the lower 40s with 
some patchy frost being possible across our northern zones. 
Temperatures will rebound a bit by Wednesday and Thursday with 
daytime highs warming back into the mid-upper 70s.
